data.assessment: In this quiet period under v2 (sanction_lambda 1.0), service is at its ceiling: 87.2 of 87.4 orders were on time, with 0.2 late, 0 unfinished, a lowest company on-time rate of 0.99 and a worst-company p95 wait of 81.2 s. At most 0.2 on-time deliveries can still be gained, below the constitution's min_improvement of 1.0, so no rule amendment can pass the improvement gate. Contract loosening would only inflate the count without helping customers, and no vote or invariant is blocking a customer-beneficial change. One thing to watch is the doubled sanction weight: C carries almost all penalties (22.6, almost all from deadline:release overstays). Its utility is 8.4 against A's 27.4 and B's 28.8, which may harden C's votes in busier periods. This is a company-utility issue, not a customer KPI shortfall, so I propose no change this period.
